design_rationale: Explicit individual random allocation 1:1 via central block randomisation (block size eight) stratified by country, in a double-blind, placebo-controlled trial registered as NCT03671109.

domain_judgments.rationale: Central block randomisation stratified by country with allocation concealed in sealed opaque envelopes opened only after recruitment, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Allocation of participants to study groups was done centrally by the trial's sponsor ... by block randomisation of eight and stratified by country ... Study number allocation for each study participant was concealed in sealed opaque envelopes that were opened only after recruitment."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and all personnel were masked, study drug and placebo were identically packaged, dosing was directly observed, and the primary analysis used a modified intention-to-treat population (with supportive per-protocol analysis).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Study drug tablets (dihydroartemisinin–piperaquine and placebo) were identically packaged. All study personnel, investigators, outcome assessors, data analysts, and participants remained masked to treatment assignment throughout the trial."

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were available for 602 of 666 (90%) randomised women with near-identical proportions missing in each group (294/332 vs 308/334), making bias from missingness unlikely, although the extremely low event rate means interpretation rests on very few events.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Peripheral blood samples were collected at delivery from 602 (90%) of 666 participants, thus contributing to the primary endpoint analysis"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (microscopy-detected P falciparum parasitaemia) is objective, measured identically in both groups using standardised quality-controlled laboratory procedures, with outcome assessors masked to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Plasmodium falciparum parasites were identified by microscopy on Giemsa-stained blood films according to standard, quality-controlled procedures."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered with a published protocol and the pre-specified primary outcome is clearly reported as null, but the headline positive conclusions rest substantially on explicitly post-hoc composite outcomes, raising some concern about selective emphasis among multiple analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Post-hoc analyses (not prespecified in the protocol) were done for (1) malaria infection during study follow-up ... and (2) overall malaria or anaemia at delivery"

overall_summary: This well-conducted, registered, double-blind placebo-controlled trial has low risk in the randomisation, deviations, missing data, and outcome measurement domains. Overall judgment is "some concerns", driven by D5: the key reported benefits derive from explicitly post-hoc composite outcomes while the pre-specified primary endpoint was null (and severely underpowered due to unexpectedly low malaria prevalence).

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a double-blinded, randomized, placebo-controlled trial in which 200 HIV-infected pregnant women were randomly assigned 1:1 using permuted variable-sized blocks of 4 and 6, with allocation handled by pharmacists not otherwise involved in the study (NCT02282293).

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was generated by variable-sized permuted blocks and concealed by independent pharmacists who prepared identical-appearing active and placebo drugs; baseline characteristics were broadly balanced, and the single borderline imbalance in primigravidity (13% vs 5%, P = .05) across many compared variables is consistent with chance and was addressed by gravidity-adjusted analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Women were randomly assigned to receive standard chemoprevention with daily TMP-SMX plus monthly placebo or daily TMP-SMX plus monthly DP in a 1:1 ratio, using permuted variable-sized blocks of 4 and 6. Pharmacists not otherwise involved in the study were responsible for treatment allocation and the preparation of study drugs."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, care providers and outcome assessors were blinded by use of an identical-appearing placebo, the first dose of each course was directly observed, protocol-driven discontinuations (switch to protease inhibitor) still had outcomes ascertained, and a modified intention-to-treat analysis was used; the only minor uncertainty is unmeasured adherence to the home-administered second and third doses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Participants randomly assigned to receive daily TMP-SMX alone were given DP placebo with the same appearance and number of tablets as active DP... All analyses were done using a modified intention-to-treat approach including all women allocated to treatment with evaluable outcomes of interest."

domain_judgments.rationale: There was no loss to follow-up and the primary outcome was available for 97% of randomized women (96/100 and 98/100), with similar, very small amounts of missingness in each arm, so bias from missing data is implausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All 200 women enrolled were followed through delivery, and 194 (97%) had placental tissue collected for histopathologic analysis"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome used an objective, standardized histopathologic definition assessed identically in both arms by duplicate blinded readers with third-reader adjudication, and blood smears/LAMP had similar quality-control and blinding procedures.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Slides prepared for histopathologic analysis were read in duplicate, using a standardized case record form, by 2 independent readers... and any discrepant results were resolved by a third reader... Readers were blinded to both treatment assignment and findings of prior reads."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a single clearly pre-specified primary outcome and an a priori power calculation, and the full set of pre-stated secondary efficacy, tolerability and safety outcomes (including null and unfavourable findings such as the QT increase) is reported, with the adjusted gravidity analysis presented transparently alongside the unadjusted result.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Clinical Trials Registration. NCT02282293." ... "The primary outcome was the prevalence of placental malarial infection, based on the presence of any parasites or malaria pigment detected by histopathologic analysis."

overall_summary: All five RoB 2 domains were judged at low risk: a prospectively registered, double-blinded, placebo-controlled trial with concealed block randomization by independent pharmacists, complete follow-up (97% primary outcome ascertainment), blinded duplicate histopathologic outcome assessment, and modified intention-to-treat analysis of pre-specified outcomes. The main interpretive caveat is not bias but low statistical power/precision, since the observed event rate (3.1% in the control arm) was far below the 20% assumed in the sample size calculation following indoor residual spraying, making the null result imprecise rather than biased.

design_rationale: The paper describes an individually randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled multicenter trial: "The allocation of the participants to the study arms was done centrally by block randomization (block size of 6) stratified by country", with a computer-generated randomization list held by an independent pharmacy department; registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT00811421).

domain_judgments.rationale: Central computer-generated stratified block randomization with concealed, sequentially numbered opaque envelopes opened only after recruitment, and baseline characteristics (Table 1) were closely balanced between arms, consistent with chance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The allocation of the participants to the study arms was done centrally by block randomization (block size of 6) stratified by country... The Pharmacy Department of the Hospital Clinic in Barcelona produced and safeguarded the computer-generated randomization list for each recruiting site until unblinding... Study number allocation for each participant was concealed in opaque sealed envelopes that were sequentially numbered and opened only after recruitment"

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blinding with an identical-appearing placebo and an ITT primary analysis are strengths, but the markedly higher rate of MQ-specific adverse effects (29.6% dizziness, 23.9% vomiting) could have functionally unblinded participants/providers, and non-receipt of the 2nd/3rd doses was somewhat more frequent in the MQ arm; the co-primary reliance on ATP analyses for several key findings (viral load, MTCT) is not intention-to-treat.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Investigators, laboratory staff, care providers, and study participants were blinded to intervention throughout the study... The second IPTp dose was not given to 4.7% and 7.8% of women who had received the first dose of placebo and MQ, respectively. The third dose was not given to 7.5% and 10.6% of the women who had received the second dose of placebo and MQ"

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary endpoint data were available for 973/1,071 (~91%) with balanced losses across arms, but some outcomes had more substantial missingness (e.g., gestational age at birth available for only 436/1,071; viral load "no data" in ~13% per arm; MTCT analysis N=855) and no sensitivity analyses for missingness were reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of 973 peripheral blood samples from women at delivery were collected (490 from control and 483 from MQ group)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary and key secondary outcomes were objective laboratory measures (microscopy/PCR parasitemia, placental histology, HIV DNA PCR, viral load) assessed identically in both arms by blinded laboratory staff.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Plasmodium falciparum parasites were identified by microscopy on Giemsa-stained blood films according to standard, quality-controlled procedures... Investigators, laboratory staff, care providers, and study participants were blinded to intervention throughout the study."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was pre-registered with an available protocol and statistical analysis plan and states all protocol outcomes are reported (low concern for the pre-specified primary endpoint), but the prominent MTCT/viral-load findings arose from post hoc exploratory analyses with data-driven covariate selection and dual ITT/ATP reporting, creating potential for selective reporting of those results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The main limitation of the latter finding relates to the exploratory nature of this part of the analysis... The unexpected finding of increased viral loads in women in the MQ group led us to conduct an exploratory analysis of the association of MTCT of HIV by group and of the factors associated with it."

overall_summary: This well-conducted, pre-registered, double-blind placebo-controlled multicenter trial has a robust randomization procedure and objective, blinded outcome measurement, so the primary malaria endpoint is at low risk of bias. Overall judgment is "some concerns" because of possible functional unblinding from MQ's distinctive adverse-effect profile with slightly unequal dose completion, moderate and variable missing outcome data for some endpoints, and reliance on post hoc exploratory ATP analyses for the headline HIV viral-load and mother-to-child-transmission findings.

design_rationale: Explicit individual random allocation: "Pregnant women living with HIV ... were randomly assigned (1:1) by computer-generated block randomisation, stratified by site and HIV status", in a two-arm, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial (NCT04158713).

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated permuted-block sequence created by an independent statistician, concealed in sequentially numbered sealed opaque envelopes containing pre-packed identical-appearing study drug, and baseline characteristics (including baseline malaria prevalence, 17% in both arms) were closely balanced.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Balanced randomisation was done using computer-generated permuted block randomisation stratified by site and HIV status ... An independent statistician not involved in the study generated the randomisation list for the trial pharmacists ... who prepared sequentially numbered, sealed, opaque envelopes for each participant with the randomisation assignments."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants, investigators and staff were masked with identical-appearing placebo, both groups received identical co-trimoxazole background care and comparable numbers of IPTp courses (median 5 in each group), and the primary analysis was a modified intention-to-treat analysis including 99% of randomised participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Placebo tablets had the same appearance as active dihydroartemisinin–piperaquine tablets ... All investigators, laboratory staf, data analysts, and participants were masked to treatment assignment ... The primary analysis was by modified intention to treat."

domain_judgments.rationale: 895/904 (99%) randomised participants contributed primary endpoint data, missingness was balanced across arms, and a non-responder imputation sensitivity analysis gave similar results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "895 (99%) participants contributed to the primary endpoint analysis ... The proportion of eligible participants with missing primary endpoint data was equally distributed across study groups ... a sensitivity analysis using non-responder imputation with missing endpoint data imputed."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was objective laboratory-detected Plasmodium infection (PCR, microscopy, RDT, placental histology) measured identically in both arms, with laboratory staff and outcome assessors masked to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All outcome assessors were masked to the treatment groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered (NCT04158713) with a published protocol and a DSMB-approved prespecified statistical analysis plan, and post-hoc analyses are explicitly labelled; the primary endpoint result is reported as prespecified (multiplicity for secondary endpoints is acknowledged but does not affect the primary result).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All analyses were prespecified (unless otherwise indicated as post hoc) in a statistical analysis plan approved by the data and safety monitoring board ... This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04158713."

overall_summary: All five RoB 2 domains were judged low risk: adequately concealed computer-generated block randomisation with balanced baseline characteristics, double-blind placebo control with modified ITT analysis, 99% primary outcome completeness, objective masked laboratory outcome ascertainment, and prospective registration with a prespecified analysis plan. Minor caveats (unsupervised home dosing, self-reported adherence, unadjusted multiplicity for secondary endpoints) do not materially threaten the primary efficacy estimate.

design_rationale: The paper reports two parallel open-label randomized controlled noninferiority trials with stratified randomization and central allocation ("In each trial, randomization was stratified according to the study site and the number of previous pregnancies... The study coordination center retained the master list and assigned treatments by phone").

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization was stratified by site and gravidity with the allocation list held centrally and treatments assigned by phone (concealed allocation), and baseline characteristics were similar between arms within each trial, although the exact sequence-generation method is not described.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In each trial, randomization was stratified according to the study site and the number of previous pregnancies (primigravid vs. multigravid). The study coordination center retained the master list and assigned treatments by phone." ... "within each trial, populations were similar in the 2 treatment groups"

domain_judgments.rationale: The trials were open-label so participants and investigators knew the assigned regimen (relevant especially for self-reported adverse events and adherence), and some deviations occurred (protocol violations, MQ discontinuations, 11% deviation in the CNM trial), though a modified ITT analysis including all randomized women with the outcome was performed and corroborated by per-protocol and sensitivity analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This trial was blinded only to the microscopists who evaluated blood smears." ... "Deviations in the administration of the allocated treatment concerned 12 women (11% of the mITT population) and 8 women (3%)"

domain_judgments.rationale: About 20–23% of randomized women lacked the primary end point (placental smear), which is substantial; although missingness was balanced across arms and differed only by timing of HIV diagnosis, loss to follow-up was acknowledged to be concentrated in CTX-alone groups, and a missing=failure analysis was not used as the main analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "despite extensive effort, placental blood was not collected in 20% of the randomized women" ... "most of the women who were lost to follow-up belonged to the CTX-alone treatment groups"

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome (microscopic placental parasitemia) is objective, read identically in both arms by two independent blinded microscopists with third-reader conciliation, so knowledge of allocation is unlikely to have influenced it (secondary/AE outcomes were unblinded, but the primary end point was protected).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "thick and thin blood smears were stained with Giemsa and read by 2 independent microscopists, with conciliation of discrepancies by a third reader" ... "Possible classification bias inherent to open-label design was minimized in our trial, thanks to its objective primary end point and the blind laboratory processing of samples."

domain_judgments.rationale: A pre-specified protocol with a defined primary end point, noninferiority margin and both mITT and PP analyses existed and a DSMB oversaw interim analysis, but no trial registration number is cited, PCR end points were added by protocol amendment after the fact, and the trial stopped before reaching target sample size with post hoc conditional power analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Malarial infections detected by PCR in placental and peripheral blood at delivery were added as secondary end points after a protocol amendment." ... "As this sample size could not be achieved after a 2-year recruitment period, we conducted conditional power and error analyses"

overall_summary: Allocation was centrally concealed and the objective primary outcome was assessed by blinded microscopists, but the open-label design, ~20% missing placental end-point data (with loss to follow-up concentrated in CTX-alone arms), truncated recruitment in the CNM trial, and post hoc addition of PCR end points without a cited registration raise some concerns. No domain reaches high risk, so the overall judgment is "some concerns".
